target: p1, n7, t1, o1, k70, k67, doc1, proposedSlots.specialised_commercial_court_installed
claim: The record says no text fixes the seats or installation of the specialised commercial courts (k70 searchedNotFound, o1) and lets a lawyer exempt p1 by answering that 'the specialised commercial court whose area covers the dispute' is not installed. Two executive decrees govern this: ED 23-53 of 14 January 2023 divided the whole national territory among twelve specialised commercial courts, and ED 26-133 of 30 March 2026 (JO 27 of 12 April 2026) raised them to twenty-five, set their installation as gradual, and extended the territorial jurisdiction of the courts installed before it to the area of each new court until that court is installed (new art. 2 مكرر 1), keeping pending procedures with the court already seized (art. 2 مكرر 2). Since April 2026, then, a dispute in the area of a new court that is not yet installed still belongs to an installed specialised commercial court. A lawyer in such an area (for example Batna, which ED 26-133 gives its own court but which ED 23-53 placed under Sétif) who truthfully answers 'no' to the slot question gets p1 exempted, doc1 not required, and n7's message that the commercial section stays competent: he may file before the commercial section, or before the specialised court, without the prior conciliation.

source.what: Executive Decree 26-133 of 11 Chaoual 1447 / 30 March 2026 amending and completing Executive Decree 23-53, arts. 2, 2 مكرر, 2 مكرر 1, 2 مكرر 2 and annex (25 courts), JO no. 27 of 12 April 2026, pp. 10-11; Executive Decree 23-53 of 21 Joumada Ethania 1444 / 14 January 2023 fixing the territorial jurisdiction of the specialised commercial courts, arts. 2-3 and annex (12 courts covering the whole territory), JO no. 02 of 15 January 2023, p. 19. Both issued under Organic Law 22-10 art. 28 and the CPCA.

quoteArabic: المادة 2 مكرر : تنصب المحاكم التجارية المتخصصة الجديدة تدريجيا، عند توفر جميع الشروط الضرورية لسيرها. المادة 2 مكرر 1 : يمتد الاختصاص الإقليمي للمحاكم التجارية المتخصصة المنصبة قبل صدور هذا المرسوم، إلى دائرة الاختصاص الإقليمي للمحاكم التجارية المتخصصة الجديدة إلى حين تنصيب هذه الأخيرة. المادة 2 مكرر 2 : تبقى الإجراءات القائمة أمام المحاكم التجارية المتخصصة المختصة قبل صدور هذا المرسوم، من اختصاص نفس هذه الجهة القضائية دون تحويلها إلى المحكمة التجارية المتخصصة الجديدة، المختصة إقليميا. — (ED 23-53) المادة 2 : يحدد عدد المحاكم التجارية المتخصصة باثنتي عشرة (12) محكمة عبر كامل التراب الوطني، تحدد دوائر اختصاصها الإقليمي طبقا للملحق المرفق بهذا المرسوم.
consequence: The installation exemption of p1 and boundary n7 should not turn on whether the court named for the lawyer's own area is installed: after ED 26-133 an installed specialised court covers every area of a new court not yet installed. The record should cite ED 23-53 and ED 26-133, replace or reword the installation slot (which specialised court currently covers the area, per the annex and art. 2 مكرر 1), point t1 to the decree annex rather than to the general territorial rules alone, turn k70 from searchedNotFound into a cited text, and regrade o1. It should also handle a conciliation requested before the older court when the new court is installed in between (art. 2 مكرر 2 keeps 'الإجراءات القائمة' with the court seized; whether that covers the conciliation step and where the claim is then filed is unsettled). Caveat: the decrees do not list which of the twelve 2023 courts were actually installed; ED 26-133 only states that some were installed and had pending procedures before 12 April 2026.

claim: In intellectual-property disputes, which p1 sends through the prior conciliation, the intellectual-property ordinances put a short deadline on the holder who obtained a seizure: under Ordinance 03-06 (trade marks) art. 35, a description or seizure ordered by the president of the court is null of right unless the plaintiff takes the civil or criminal route within one month, and under Ordinance 03-05 (copyright) art. 149 the beneficiary of conservatory measures must bring the matter before the competent court within thirty days. The prior conciliation of cpca 536 مكرر 4 may take five days to designate a judge plus up to three months before the claim can be entered. The record has no deadline, warning, boundary or open point on this clash (o4 covers only urgent applications), so a lawyer who follows p1 and waits for the record of non-conciliation can lose the seizure.

source.what: Ordinance 03-06 of 19 July 2003 on trade marks, arts. 34-35 (JO no. 44 of 23 July 2003, p. 27); Ordinance 03-05 of 19 July 2003 on copyright and related rights, arts. 147-149 (same issue, p. 20). Later amendments of these ordinances not checked (the ledger does not cover them).

quoteArabic: (الأمر 03-06) المادة 35 : يعد الوصف أو الحجز باطلا بقوة القانون إذا لم يلتمس المدعي الطريق المدني أو الجزائي خلال أجل شهر و ذلك بصرف النظر عن تعويضات الأضرار التي يمكن طلبها. — (الأمر 03-05) المادة 149 : يجب على المستفيد من التدابير التحفظية المذكورة أعلاه أن يقوم خلال الثلاثين (30) يوما ابتداء من تاريخ الأمرين المنصوص عليهما في المادتين 146 و147 من هذا الأمر بإخطار الجهة القضائية المختصة.
consequence: For intellectual-property matters the record should ask whether a description, seizure or conservatory measure was ordered and when, and warn that the one-month (marks) or thirty-day (copyright) period runs from that order while the prior conciliation may last more than three months. Whether a request for conciliation under 536 مكرر 4 counts as taking the civil route or seizing the competent court is not settled by either text: it should be an open point with a protective reading (for example, warn that the seizure may lapse and that the criminal route or another step within the period may be needed), not silence.

claim: The slot question and accepted means m1 require a record of non-conciliation 'signed by that judge, the parties and the clerk'. Paragraph 1 only makes the requesting party notify the other parties of the session date. In the common case where the other party is notified and does not come, no record can carry his signature, and neither paragraph 2 nor paragraph 3 says what record then satisfies the requirement. The record does not handle this case. A lawyer holding a record signed by the judge, the clerk and his own client, recording that the other party did not appear, must answer the slot 'no' as worded, and p1 blocks the clean export. Or he answers 'yes' with nothing telling him to check that the record states the failure. Either way, the most frequent outcome of a contested conciliation is left without an answer.

source.what: Law 22-13 of 12 July 2022 amending the CPCA, art. 3 inserting art. 536 مكرر 4 ¶1-¶3, JO no. 48 of 17 July 2022, p. 4 (same wording as the store's b25-b27).

quoteArabic: ويبلغ طالب الصلح باقي أطراف النزاع بتاريخ جلسة الصلح. ... لإجراء الصلح الذي ينتهي بتحرير محضر يوقع من القاضي وأطراف النزاع وأمين الضبط ... في حالة فشل محاولة الصلح، ترفع الدعوى ... مرفقة، تحت طائلة عدم قبول الدعوى شكلا، بمحضر عدم الصلح.
consequence: Add the case of a duly notified party who does not attend: the slot question should not make a record without the absent party's signature count as no record. A record of failure that notes the absence should satisfy p1, at least as a warning rather than a block, or the case should become an open point with a stated protective reading. Add a worked example for it.

claim: Under 536 مكرر 4 the conciliation is held among 'the parties to the dispute', who are notified by the requesting party and sign the record. The record asks only whether a record of non-conciliation exists. It never asks whether every defendant named in the petition took part in that conciliation. Common cases are a bank suing a trader and his guarantor, a maritime claim against the carrier and its insurer, or a partner dispute in which another partner or the company is added. A record of non-conciliation against defendant A then lets the petition against A and B export clean, although the claim against B is exposed to inadmissibility in form.

source.what: Law 22-13 of 12 July 2022, art. 536 مكرر 4 ¶1-¶3 of the CPCA, JO no. 48 of 17 July 2022, p. 4.

quoteArabic: يسبق قيد الدعوى إجراء الصلح الذي يتم بطلب من أحد الخصوم ... ويبلغ طالب الصلح باقي أطراف النزاع بتاريخ جلسة الصلح ... محضر يوقع من القاضي وأطراف النزاع وأمين الضبط
consequence: Ask whether every defendant of the petition was a party to the conciliation that produced the record, and warn when one was not. Treating it as a block would go beyond the text, since the text does not say whether the step is owed per defendant. Add a worked example with two defendants.

claim: p1 is required whenever specialised_commercial_matter is bankruptcy_settlement. But judicial settlement and bankruptcy proceedings are opened on the debtor's own declaration of cessation of payments, which the Commercial Code obliges him to make within fifteen days, or by the court of its own motion, as well as on a creditor's summons. In the first two there is no opposing party with whom a conciliation 'requested by one of the parties' and notified to 'the other parties' could be held. The record would block the clean export of such a filing for lack of a record of non-conciliation, and its examples (ex8, exR3) only cover the creditor-debtor case.

source.what: Own memory of the Commercial Code (Ordinance 75-59 of 26 September 1975), Book III, arts. 215 (debtor's declaration within fifteen days) and 216 (opening on a creditor's summons or by the court of its own motion). These articles are not in the store (it holds commercial-code 30 and 169 to 202 only) and were not checked on joradp.dz, nor was any later amendment of Book III.

quoteArabic: (from memory, unverified) يجب على المدين أن يدلي بإقرار في مدة خمسة عشر يوما قصد افتتاح إجراءات التسوية القضائية أو الإفلاس في حالة توقفه عن الدفع
consequence: Distinguish, within bankruptcy_settlement, a creditor's claim against the debtor (p1 applies) from the debtor's own declaration or an opening by the court (no adverse party; p1 should not block, at most warn). Fetch arts. 215-216 of the Commercial Code to confirm the wording and current version.

claim: k2's note says that the public-order exclusion of cpca 994 ¶1 is stated for mediation, not for conciliation, so conciliation is open 'in any matter and every stage'. The Civil Code chapter on the contract of compromise (arts. 459-466, absent from the store, o6) forbids compromise on matters of personal status or public order, and allows it only on the financial interests that arise from personal status. The 'any matter' of cpca 4 and 990 is therefore bounded by a text of substantive law that the record does not cite.

source.what: Own memory of Civil Code (Ordinance 75-58 of 26 September 1975) art. 461. Not read on the Official Journal in this run: both fetches of JO no. 78 of 1975 failed and were not retried in a loop. Whether art. 461 was later amended was not checked (the ledger lists no instrument touching arts. 459-466).

quoteArabic: (from memory, unverified) لا يجوز الصلح في المسائل المتعلقة بالحالة الشخصية أو بالنظام العام، ولكن يجوز الصلح على المصالح المالية الناجمة عن الحالة الشخصية.
consequence: k2's answer and note should not suggest that a conciliation may settle a public-order or personal-status question. They should cite Civil Code 461 once it is fetched, and o6 should name this article. This has no effect on the petition gates.

claim: The record says that the regulation cpca 998 ¶5 refers to is not in the store. It answers k55 (how the mediator is paid, deposit) as not found and keeps o9 at grade D. That regulation exists: Executive Decree 09-100 of 10 March 2009, taken expressly in application of cpca 998. It provides that judicial mediators are chosen from lists drawn up at each Court (art. 4). The appointing judge fixes the mediator's fees and may grant an advance on them. Unless the parties agree otherwise, they bear the fees in equal shares, or as the judge decides in view of their social situation (art. 12).

source.what: Executive Decree 09-100 of 13 Rabie El Aouel 1430 / 10 March 2009 fixing the modalities of designation of the judicial mediator, arts. 1, 4, 12, 13, JO no. 16 of 15 March 2009, Arabic p. 5. Later amendments not checked.

quoteArabic: المادة 12 : يتقاضى الوسيط القضائي مقابل أتعاب، يحدد مقداره القاضي الذي عينه. يمكن الوسيط القضائي أن يطلب من القاضي تسبيقا، يخصم من أتعابه النهائية. يتحمل الأطراف مناصفة مقابل أتعاب الوسيط القضائي، ما لم يتفقوا على خلاف ذلك أو ما لم يقرر القاضي خلاف ذلك بالنظر إلى الوضعية الاجتماعية للأطراف.
consequence: Answer k55 and o9 from ED 09-100: fees are fixed by the appointing judge, an advance may be granted, and the parties bear them equally unless they agree otherwise or the judge decides otherwise. Mediators are taken from lists at each Court. Drop grade D on o9. This has no effect on the petition.
